conviction_note: Q3 revenue is effectively pre-released (99,964 deliveries at the top of a 95-100k guide, Street already at the top of the RMB26.6-28.0bn revenue range), so the print turns on gross margin (one broker at 16.7% vs a ~RMB942M consensus loss that implies ~13%) and on the first Q4 guide (i6 ramp to 20k/month against a domestic NEV market down 13% YoY in early November); the stock is at its 52-week low after -8% in five days, with roughly 10 days to cover, and its own six confirmed prints moved a median ~1.8%. The findings sum to +1.3, and the scaled number is +0.4 (p_up 54 x abs 5.0). The gap is the put skew (+12.6 vol points) and an unsourced Q4 bar, which hold p_up near 50 while the individual findings lean up.
bar: Q3 revenue consensus about US$4.09bn (Earnings Whispers preview via Finviz, 2026-11-18, https://finviz.com/news/424957/li-auto-needs-margin-proof-as-street-bets-on-the-top-of-its-revenue-guide), which is roughly RMB27.5bn at 6.715 and sits at the top of the company's RMB26.6-28.0bn guide (https://cnevpost.com/2026/11/10/li-auto-q3-2026-results-nov-25/). EPS consensus is a loss of US$0.08 per ADS (same Finviz source). Net-loss consensus is RMB942M against Deutsche Bank's RMB300M (CnEVPost 2026-11-10). Chartmill shows revenue of RMB28.2bn and an EPS loss of CN¥1.98, which disagrees on EPS sign and scale. No sourced consensus for Q4 deliveries, Q4 revenue or gross margin, so the guidance findings are capped small.
positioning_check: US short interest is about 29.1-29.2M ADS (ShortSqueeze late Oct 2026, 9.3 days to cover; Fintel 12.2 days to cover; AltIndex 3.63% of shares outstanding as of 2026-08-14), via https://altindex.com/ticker/li/short-interest, https://fintel.io/s/us/LI and https://shortsqueeze.com/?symbol=LI. Against the baseline's 20-day average volume of 2.89M that is about 10 days to cover, a crowded short in days even though it is small in percent of shares. Bloomberg reported record Hong Kong shorts in January 2026 (https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-01-23/li-auto-shorts-climb-to-record-as-ev-competition-intensifies). Baseline: 25-delta skew is +12.56 vol points (puts bid, downside paid), the event-implied move is 5.95% (ATM spread is 67% of mid, so indicative only), put/call open interest is 0.97, spot is 2.4% above the 52-week low and 46.9% below the high, and the 5-day run-up is -8.0%. Most of that came on 2026-11-20, when LI fell 7.6% (11.24 to 10.39 on 4.6M volume) while XPEV fell 13.9% and KWEB 2.8% (Yahoo chart bars). That was a sector move with no Li-specific cause found.

findings.finding: Q3 deliveries were 99,964, at the top of the company's 95,000-100,000 guide (+7.2% YoY, +1.7% QoQ), so Q3 revenue should land near the top of the RMB26.6-28.0bn guide, about RMB27.8-28.0bn, against a consensus of about US$4.09bn (~RMB27.5bn) that Earnings Whispers says already sits 'essentially at the top' of the range. Revenue is effectively pre-released and a slight beat at most (Deutsche Bank models only RMB27.0bn).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: My rebuild from confirmed bmo releases (Yahoo daily closes, close before to close of print day): Q4'24 2025-03-14 -4.4%; Q1'25 2025-05-29 +2.1%; Q2'25 2025-08-28 +2.9%; Q3'25 2025-11-26 +0.6%; Q1'26 2026-05-28 -1.5%; Q2'26 2026-08-26 -1.1%. On Q2'26 a revenue beat (RMB25.67bn vs RMB25.07bn) was outweighed by a weak guide (-1.3% premarket, -1.1% close).
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced. Deliveries were published on Oct 1 and the Street moved to the top of the guide. If the market expected a revenue miss, consensus would sit mid-range or below; it sits at the top.
findings.independence: Consensus level and the 'top of range' framing: https://finviz.com/news/424957/li-auto-needs-margin-proof-as-street-bets-on-the-top-of-its-revenue-guide (2026-11-18). Shares the delivery number with every other finding.

findings.finding: Q3 gross margin is the swing line. Q2 was 11.0% (vehicle margin 9.4%). Deutsche Bank (2026-11-10) forecasts 16.7% and a RMB300M net loss against a RMB942M consensus loss. Backing out Q2's cost structure (opex ~RMB5.1bn, ~RMB0.6bn other income), the consensus loss implies a gross margin near 13%. Supports for a step-up: the CFO said in August that H2 margins would expand on Livis mix, the refreshed BEV L6 and the RMB369,800 i9 (on sale 2026-09-16, 2,206 delivered in September); DB cites the removal of cash subsidies on the old L6; and XPeng's vehicle margin rose 1.0pt QoQ to 13.1% on mix in the same quarter. Headwind: higher battery, memory-chip and PCB costs that management said it would not pass on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1'26 margin collapse (GM 7.9% vs 17.8% prior quarter): -1.5% on the print day. Q2'26 margin recovery to 11.0% (+3.1pt QoQ): -1.1%, with guidance dominating. The stock has not paid much for margin surprises on the print day.
findings.why_not_priced: The DB number is public but is one broker. Consensus still carries a RMB942M loss and the EW preview names margin as the open question ('a margin stalling near 11% would suggest cost pressure'). If the market had adopted DB's view, consensus EPS would be near break-even rather than -US$0.08, and puts would not be bid at +12.6 vol points into the print.
findings.independence: CFO's H2 margin-expansion guide on the Q2 call: https://cnevpost.com/2026/08/26/li-auto-earnings-q2-2026/. Peer mix read-through, XPeng Q3 vehicle margin 13.1% vs 12.1%: https://cnevpost.com/2026/11/16/xpeng-q3-2026-earnings. The cost headwind is in the same Q2 call transcript: https://www.webull.com/news/15469407170544640.

findings.finding: Q4 delivery guide, i6 ramp side. October was 29,025 (lowest since February). The updated i6 (launched 2026-10-28, RMB239,800 intro price to Nov 30) has an estimated 50,000+ orders and 9-11 week dealer wait times. Capacity goes to 20,000/month in November and higher in December, and DB expects November deliveries above 40,000 (16-20k i6). On those numbers a Q4 guide around 110-125k is plausible, against 109,194 in Q4 2025 (flat to up YoY, the first growth since early 2026). Management said on the Q2 call that positive operating and free cash flow 'will largely depend on our fourth-quarter deliveries'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name trades on the guide. Q2'26: Q3 revenue guide of RMB26.6-28.0bn vs ~RMB32.3bn consensus, stock -1.1%. Q3'25: Q4'25 guide of 100-110k vs ~138k expected, stock +0.6% on the day, because it was already washed out. Peer read on the same line: XPeng guided Q4 deliveries ~7% above Goldman's expectation on 2026-11-16 and rose 3-5% that day.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The DB order estimate is public, but November deliveries are not published until Dec 1, and Li Auto stopped putting out a usable weekly series, so the market has no company figure for the ramp. A sell-side that had adopted a 40k+ November would not have the stock at a 52-week low with puts bid. The Q4 bar is unsourced, so this is capped small.
findings.independence: Company statements on the i6 capacity plan (20k in November, more in December) and 7-8 week waits as of Oct 30: https://cnevpost.com/2026/11/01/li-auto-oct-2026-deliveries/. i9 above 10,000 cumulative deliveries 58 days after launch (Oct 5,460): https://cnevpost.com/2026/11/13/li-auto-i9-tops-10000-deliveries. Shares the DB note with the margin finding, but on a different line.

findings.finding: Q4 delivery guide, demand side. The domestic market is weak. CPCA: NEV retail for Nov 1-15 2026 was 447k, -13% YoY (Nov 1-8 had been -7%), after October NEV retail of 1.148M (-10% YoY). Li Auto's Jan-Oct deliveries are 322,461 (-2.0% YoY), and the ~490k full-year figure referenced around the Q2 call is out of reach (it would need ~197-202k in Q4). Hong Kong auto stocks fell on Nov 12-13 on weak domestic demand and a cautious Citi view. This weighs on how far the i6 ramp can lift the guide and on the L-series EREV base.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4'25 guide (100-110k vs ~138k expected) was a large miss and the stock barely moved (+0.6%) because expectations had already reset. The market-wide weakness is visible in the sector tape (LI -7.6%, XPEV -13.9% on 2026-11-20).
findings.source_date: 2026-11-18 (CPCA Nov 1-15 release as reported in search; the URL path dates the stockstar item 2026-11-11 for the Nov 1-8 data)
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it is a public industry series and the stock is -8% in five days at a 52-week low. It is filed because it is the broad series the i6-ramp finding has to beat (lesson 5), not because the market missed it. It is an industry proxy and the company has not confirmed the transmission.
findings.independence: Proxy, not company data. Li Auto's own October (-8.6% YoY): https://cnevpost.com/2026/11/01/li-auto-oct-2026-deliveries/. Q2 call full-year arithmetic: https://cnevpost.com/2026/08/26/li-auto-earnings-q2-2026/. HK sector selling on Nov 12-13 (search summary of www.cls.cn / stockstar 2026-11-13).

findings.finding: Cost inflation the company chose to absorb. On the Q2 call management said memory chip, PCB and battery raw-material costs had risen and that it 'made a decision not to pass these price increases over to our customers'. It still holds a long-run 'healthy' gross margin of 15-20% with no timeline. Any Q4 margin commentary pointing to renewed compression (Xiaomi has warned of heavier memory pressure) would hurt the outlook read.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Li Auto does not formally guide margin. Margin-driven drawdowns in 2026 came around launches (May 2026, -18% over two HK sessions after the L9 launch on price and profit concerns), not on print days.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely known: DB's 16.7% already nets these costs, and the EW preview flags them. Filed small as the counterweight to the margin finding. The crowded short (about 10 days to cover) argues against sizing a negative larger.
findings.independence: Xiaomi on memory costs as a component headwind (Q2 2026): https://thenextweb.com/news/xiaomi-q2-2026-earnings-memory-crunch. The EW preview lists the same headwind: https://finviz.com/news/424957/li-auto-needs-margin-proof-as-street-bets-on-the-top-of-its-revenue-guide.

findings.finding: Li Mega supply problem. Samsung's custom 29-inch 6K OLED is short until about year-end, so Megas built Nov 10 to Dec 17 ship with the L9 Livis LCD. Li Auto will swap in the OLED free from 2027-03-01 and is reported to be adding a three-year service package. That points to a Q4 warranty or service accrual and possibly some softer Mega orders. The scale is small: Mega volume was 3,000+ in October.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2025 Mega recall cost cut Q3'25 vehicle margin from 19.8% ex-item to 16.3%. On that print the stock rose 0.6%: one-offs have been looked through.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since Nov 2 and small. The cost would only show if management quantifies a Q4 accrual or names Mega supply in the guide, which nobody models.
findings.independence: Chinese coverage of the build window and compensation: https://wap.eastmoney.com/a/202611033920402185.html (2026-11-03).

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is washed out. Spot $10.64 is 2.4% above the 52-week low and 46.9% below the high. The stock is -8.0% in five sessions, mostly a sector-wide drop on 2026-11-20 (LI -7.6%, XPEV -13.9%, KWEB -2.8%) with no Li-specific cause found. Short interest is about 29M ADS, roughly 10 days to cover at 2.9M average volume. EW describes sentiment as 'modestly bearish'. A merely in-line print plus a non-disastrous Q4 guide can squeeze.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After the sharp pre-print selloffs into the Q3'25 print (Nov 2025, a weak guide) and the Q2'25 print (Aug 2025, -8% the day before), the print-day reactions were +0.6% and +2.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: The skew (+12.6 vol points, puts bid) says the option market leans the other way. My reason it may be wrong for this print: the downside story (weak October, weak industry) is already public and in the price at a 52-week low, the revenue line is pre-released, and with ~10 days to cover any margin beat has a squeeze mechanism. Sized small because the skew disagrees.

findings.finding: Buyback capacity. The US$1bn program (approved 2026-03-24, runs to 2027-03-31) had about US$631.5M used by the Q2 release, leaving roughly US$370M. Hong Kong buybacks look to have slowed in September (HK$51.5M on Sep 1, HK$5.6M on Sep 14, aggregator reports). Cash was RMB87.5bn at end-June. An upsized or new program with the results is possible but not signalled.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The March 2026 US$1bn program announcement (2026-03-24) coincided with +3.6% that day (17.13 to 17.75, Yahoo bars), confounded with other news.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody models an upsizing. It is filed small because no document signals one, and the slowing September pace cuts both ways.
findings.independence: Q2 call buyback tally: https://www.webull.com/news/15469407170544640. HK buybacks: https://www.itiger.com/news/1111052352.

baseline_tension: The findings lean mildly up (margin step-up per one broker, i6 ramp, washed-out positioning) against a strongly put-bid skew (+12.6 vol points) and a -8% five-day run-down. The run-down supports the long through positioning; the skew argues against it. That disagreement is why p_up is only 54 although the findings sum to +1.3.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction) plus the rebuilt reaction history (median |move| ~1.8% over six confirmed prints): margin finding +0.8 -> +0.6.
Lesson 6 (inside the guided range): Q3 revenue lands inside the company guide and is pre-released by deliveries, so +0.3 -> +0.1.
Lesson 6 (unsourced bar): there is no sourced Q4 consensus, so both guidance findings are capped: i6 ramp +1.0 -> +0.7, industry weakness -0.8 -> -0.5.
Lesson 7 (crowded short, ~10 days to cover): the cost-inflation negative shrinks -0.5 -> -0.4. The positioning finding stays at +0.8 with an explicit why-the-skew-may-be-wrong sentence.
Lesson 2 (one-offs): the Mega OLED accrual stays small at -0.2. The buyback has no signal and is trimmed +0.3 -> +0.2.

Last lesson (untrustworthy FPI history): the base rate was rebuilt from confirmed release dates using Yahoo bars and used in reaction_history. abs_move_pct stays at 5.0 (the option-implied 5.95 is indicative given the 67% spread) and is not cut further; p_up is unchanged at 54.
